Share on X Telegram Prince Harry, the Duke of Sussex, has expressed his desire to reconcile with his father, King Charles III, and other members of the British royal family after years of strained relationships.
Harry, 42, said he wanted to put past disagreements behind him, stressing that resolving family disputes was particularly important amid other challenges facing the world.
Speaking in an interview with GQ magazine, he said, “With everything else that’s going on in the world, the most important thing is to reconcile.”
Harry’s relationship with the royal family deteriorated after he and his wife, Meghan, stepped back from their royal duties and moved to California in 2020. The couple subsequently made public criticisms of the royal institution.
His relationship with his elder brother and heir to the British throne, Prince William, has also remained strained, while contact with his father has been limited in recent years.
Explaining why he believed people were interested in the family’s disagreements, Harry said their experiences reflected relationship challenges faced by many families.
“There’s sibling disagreements, there’s broken relationships between kids and their parents, kids and one parent,” he said.
According to him, efforts to resolve such disagreements could inspire others to repair their own relationships.
“And some people don’t want it to work out. I want it to work out,” he added.
However, Harry’s spokesperson clarified that the comments were not intended as a criticism of William or any other member of the royal family.
The Duke of Sussex acknowledged that reconciliation would not necessarily erase the pain caused by past disagreements but said he wanted people to move forward.
“For me, there’s enough drama in the world and enough drama in people’s lives than to continue with issues with family,” he said. “It’s not worth it.”
In the interview, Harry also reflected on the death of his mother, Princess Diana, when he was 12, as well as his mental health struggles.
He further discussed his return to Britain, saying that having his children attend a British school had been particularly meaningful to him.
“I didn’t know how important it was to me. I always thought it was going to be something that we would try and do, but now they’ve been in school for two weeks. They’re loving it and it’s just giving them a whole different experience.”
Harry also expressed hope that his troubled relationship with the British press could improve.
His disputes with sections of the British media were among the issues that contributed to tensions surrounding his departure from royal duties. He has also pursued several legal actions against newspaper groups over their reporting.
“There have been some battles that have been fought, necessarily so. But hopefully we can all draw a line under that.”
He added that he hoped to move beyond past disagreements with his family and the British press in the interest of a better future.
“As with everything else that’s going on in the world, there’s aspects of the past that I’m sure all of us, me, my family, some of the British press, that we’d all like to leave behind us and work for the greater good.”
